record.limits_note: 200 GB/dataset; 50 top-level files per dataset (use a directory tree or a ZIP. record.reliability_note: Stable, corporate-owned (Google), no history of quota clawback; the failure modes are ingestion flakiness on very large uploads and un-deletable old versions, not data loss.

record.notes: The amount is unverified by design: 'a very high complimentary compute quota' carries no number on any page read, so the record claims the mechanism and not the size. Three explanations for why the quota exists were considered: it subsidises benchmark supply for Kaggle's leaderboards, it is developer marketing for the model providers, and it replaces engineering work the labs would otherwise do. The page states the first two in its own words ('Managed infrastructure', 'Grow exposure to the Kaggle community'). The gate that matters is that the compute is scoped to evaluations, so a reader should not plan a fine-tune on it.
